body.statement: Theorem 3 (fixed-input plug-in inference). Fix one finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), fix its equality-branch circuit \(\tau\), and fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\). Every recorded denominator is positive at \(P\), so the rational circuit \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(P\), the event defining \(\widehat\tau_n\) has probability tending to one, and \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau(P))\Rightarrow\mathcal N\left(0,J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\right)\). Moreover, \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}J_{\tau}(P)\Sigma_PJ_{\tau}(P)^{\mathsf T}\). If \(\sigma_y^2>0\), then \(\widehat\tau_{n,y}\pm1.96\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,yy}/n}\) has limiting coverage \(0.95\) for \(P_x(Y=y)\).
body.justification: A certified population functional should produce standard sampling inference without graphwise duplicate estimates.
body.gap: Chang, Guo, and Malinsky handle data-driven graph selection by interval unions; this theorem instead gives pointwise plug-in inference for one fixed certified oracle, tied family, and arithmetic circuit.
body.consumer: After a population or externally certified discovery analysis, practitioners can estimate the common intervention probability with one covariance calculation.
